title: US Envoys Head to Moscow and Dublin After Abu Dhabi Talks, Scott Colom Flips Mississippi's Senate Seat, and Indonesia's Vice President Resigns
subhead: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner carry ceasefire proposals from Abu Dhabi to Vladimir Putin and Volodymyr Zelenskyy; Democrat Scott Colom becomes Mississippi's first Black US senator since Reconstruction; Indonesian Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka steps down over a degree dispute; and Pope Leo XIV returns to Peru.

sections.heading: US Envoys Carry Abu Dhabi Proposals to Putin in Moscow and Zelenskyy in Dublin
sections.body:
According to France 24, US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will travel to Moscow to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin and to Dublin to meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Thursday, building on two days of trilateral discussions in Abu Dhabi. Meanwhile, The War Zone reported that Ukrainian commanders are already expressing alarm over a White House-brokered temporary ceasefire in the strategic riverside town of Oleshky on the Dnipro River, warning that Russia is using the pause to reinforce forward positions for new river crossings. In Moscow, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov told a Collective Security Treaty Organization gathering that Russia rejects European proposals for a broader truce, claiming such pauses merely buy Kyiv time to replenish losses.

The split between Washington's shuttle diplomacy and battlefield realities along the Dnipro highlights how fragile localized freezes remain when neither army has exhausted its offensive reserves. While Zelenskyy confirmed to Bloomberg HT that negotiations toward a three-way leaders' summit are continuing, Kyiv's foreign minister simultaneously pressed US Secretary of State Marco Rubio to speed up air-defense interceptor deliveries as Russian strikes target Ukraine's winter power grid.
sections.whyItMatters: Shuttle diplomacy between Moscow and Dublin tests whether the Abu Dhabi channel can produce a durable freeze or whether local ceasefires like Oleshky simply allow Russian units to stage fresh assaults.

sections.heading: Democrat Scott Colom Wins Mississippi Senate Race in Historic Upset
sections.body:
Democrat Scott Colom defeated Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi's US Senate race, The Guardian, BBC, and AP News reported after the contest was called eight days past midterm election day. Colom becomes the first Black US senator elected from Mississippi since Reconstruction in 1874, prevailing in a deep-red state despite minimal financial backing from national Democratic committees.

Colom's narrow victory further reshapes the incoming 120th Congress, where a new Reuters/Ipsos poll cited by Defense News shows 71% of Americans want lawmakers to pass legislation ending the conflict with Iran. At the same time, AP News and NBC News reported that the White House sent letters warning congressional Democrats that planned oversight inquiries—including Senator Richard Blumenthal's probe into White House construction funding and top Democrats' demands for Trump administration records on Nvidia and China—could face criminal referrals.
sections.whyItMatters: Colom's upset expands Democratic margins in Congress just as the White House braces for subpoena battles over Iran war powers and executive branch oversight.

sections.heading: Indonesian Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka Resigns Over Education Row
sections.body:
Indonesian Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka—the eldest son of former President Joko Widodo—resigned on Wednesday following a protracted controversy over the validity of his educational qualifications, Al Jazeera reported. The dispute over his overseas secondary and university credentials had dogged his tenure since his controversial 2024 candidacy, which required a Constitutional Court age-limit exception to proceed.

In neighboring East Asia, diplomatic preparations accelerated ahead of next week's regional summits. According to the South China Morning Post, Taiwan named Acer founder Stan Shih as its envoy to the upcoming APEC leaders' summit in Shenzhen, urging Beijing to treat Taipei's delegation on an "equal footing" and with dignity. Yonhap and Anadolu Agency added that South Korean President Lee Jae Myung will travel to the Philippines and China next week to attend both the ASEAN and APEC gatherings.
sections.whyItMatters: Gibran's sudden departure upends President Prabowo Subianto's ruling coalition in Jakarta, while Taipei's choice of chip and PC pioneer Stan Shih for Shenzhen puts cross-strait protocol to an immediate test.

sections.heading: Pope Leo XIV Returns to Peru as European States Push UN Action on West Bank
sections.body:
Pope Leo XIV—the first American-born pontiff, who spent two decades as a missionary and bishop in Peru and holds Peruvian citizenship—returned to Lima to mammoth crowds, The New York Times and The Washington Post reported. He was greeted on arrival by Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori, whose late father's authoritarian policies the pontiff had publicly protested during his years in the country, shortly after an emotional farewell in Buenos Aires with Argentine President Javier Milei.

In the Middle East, Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli airstrike hit the intensive care unit at Gaza's Nasser Hospital, killing at least six people, while Anadolu Agency noted that the death of 20-year-old goalkeeper Mahmoud Abdel-Malek brought the toll among Palestinian athletes to 1,017. On the diplomatic front, The Times of Israel reported that Denmark and several European governments are pressing for an emergency UN Security Council session next week over Israeli construction plans in the West Bank's E1 corridor, even as French border police at Paris's airport denied entry to West Bank settler leader Yossi Dagan, Le Monde reported.
sections.whyItMatters: European moves to sanction settler officials at border controls and convene the UN Security Council over E1 mark a sharper break with Israeli settlement policy.

sections.heading: General Strike Draws 120,000 in Madrid as Brooklyn Building Collapse Kills Two
sections.body:
Approximately 120,000 protesters marched through rain in Madrid during Spain's first general strike since 2012, Euronews reported, rallying against soaring housing costs and household budget pressures, while clashes broke out between riot police and masked demonstrators in Barcelona. In New York City, a three-story building adjacent to a construction site partially collapsed in Flatbush, Brooklyn, killing at least two people and injuring more than a dozen, with four hospitalized in critical condition, Mayor Zohran Mamdani and fire officials told NBC News and Le Monde.

Meanwhile, in Washington, CBS News reported that US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent relocated from his private residence to military housing on a US base following intelligence warnings of Iranian threats against his life.
sections.whyItMatters: Spain's mass housing walkout underscores mounting cost-of-living anger across Western Europe, while Bessent's move onto a military base shows Iranian retaliation threats reaching top US economic officials.

bottomLine: US envoys carry Abu Dhabi truce proposals to Moscow and Dublin even as Kyiv warns the Oleshky ceasefire is aiding Russian river crossings, while Democrat Scott Colom's historic Mississippi Senate win and Indonesian Vice President Gibran's resignation reshape domestic coalitions.
sources: France 24, The War Zone, The Guardian, BBC, AP News, NBC News, Al Jazeera, South China Morning Post, Anadolu Agency, The New York Times, The Washington Post, The Times of Israel, Le Monde, Euronews, CBS News
